blocks.title: Vulnerability Response and Remediation exam shortcuts
items: Apply the update that removes the vulnerability.
Example: A critical browser flaw is fixed with the vendor patch.
Cannot patch but can isolate → SEGMENTATION
Example: A legacy device is moved to a restricted VLAN.
Preferred control cannot be used → COMPENSATING CONTROL
Use an alternative that reduces the same risk.
Example: A WAF protects an application that cannot be patched immediately.
Organization formally accepts deviation → EXCEPTION / EXEMPTION
Document the reason, scope, approval, and review period.
Example: A legacy system receives a temporary patch exception.
Need to transfer financial consequences → INSURANCE
Insurance does not remove the vulnerability, but can shift some financial risk.
Example: Cyber insurance covers certain incident costs.
blocks.example: Focus on which stage of the vulnerability-management lifecycle the scenario is describing.

questions.q: A vendor releases an update that removes a critical vulnerability. Which response is most direct?
questions.explanation: Patching applies the fix that removes the vulnerability.

questions.q: A legacy system cannot be patched, so it is moved to a restricted VLAN with limited access. Which response is being used?
questions.explanation: Segmentation reduces exposure and lateral movement when direct remediation is limited.

questions.q: An application cannot be patched immediately, so a WAF is configured to block exploit attempts. Which response is this?
questions.explanation: A compensating control is an alternative control used when the preferred fix cannot be implemented.

questions.q: A system receives formal approval to delay a required patch because of operational constraints. Which concept best fits?
questions.explanation: Exceptions and exemptions are formally approved deviations from security requirements.

questions.q: An organization purchases cyber insurance to reduce financial impact from certain incidents. Which response category is this?
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers some financial risk to an insurer.
